notes: σέβασμα's English is a finite relative clause with no participle to carry the relativizer, so the supplied that is rides with the noun, which is rule 92's anarthrous shape (κατηγορίᾳ → who are accused).
ἔστιν is left unrepresented because the ASV's setting himself forth as God writes no verb for it; a reference comparison will report this as a disagreement.
ὁ ἀντικείμενος splits under rule 32, the article keeping only he, while λεγόμενον takes its relativizer and copula under rule 31 because θεόν is an expressed head noun.
ἀποδεικνύντα → setting … forth heads on the verb word; forth reads as the particle answering to ἀπο-.
